clue.text: Way I play all the ABC

definitions.text: Way I play all the ABC

indicators.note: read as 'in a way', the following words are taken out of their order and set down afresh

explanation.surface: Someone explains their method for playing through the whole alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of I PLAY ALL THE ABC are rearranged, 'Way' signalling the shake-up, and the whole clue also describes going through the ABC in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Going through every letter from A to Z in sequence is to proceed in order of the letters.

clue.text: Rented accommodation not solely for Chanticleer's mate

parts.note: partly, i.e. not wholly or only, gives PART
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flat that is only partly rented.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanticleer is the cockerel in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale; his favourite hen is Pertelote, known in English as Dame Partlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Partlet is the traditional name of the hen who partners the cock Chanticleer in fable.

clue.text: She has an abbreviation for Wearside

parts.note: taken as written
Wearside, around Sunderland, is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A woman is said to use a short form for the Wearside area of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearside is the area around the River Wear and Sunderland in North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for any female person, here a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: One-time German moving out

indicators.note: the letters are moving about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A former German citizen is leaving the country.
explanation.walkthrough: I and T join GERMAN and the eight letters are shuffled, 'moving' signalling it; the whole clue also describes such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves their own country to settle abroad is moving out of it for good.

clue.text: Altered date that is bound to give some thought

indicators.note: the abbreviation is wrapped around the rest like a binding

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: an altered word has had its letters changed round

explanation.surface: A changed appointment ought to make someone stop and think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' turns DATE into DEAT, and 'bound' wraps IE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To form ideas or concepts in the mind is to think about something.

clue.text: Perform a breathtaking act

parts.note: a breathtaking act sounds like an astonishing show, but literally it takes someone's breath away, i.e. chokes them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathtaking' is read literally: depriving of air rather than amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother or suffocate is literally to stop someone's breathing.

clue.text: Flagging guide of the French missing inland

indicators.note: the shortened guide is placed inside the ground word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the French word is lacking from the guide, so its letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A tired French guide has wandered off somewhere inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes DE out of GUIDE, leaving GUI, and 'in' puts that inside LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone listless and lacking energy is weary and drooping.

clue.text: Work for a snob

parts.note: snob is an old word for a cobbler, so the material a cobbler works is meant, not a job for a social climber

explanation.walkthrough: Snob in its old sense means a shoemaker or cobbler, not a social climber.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide used for soles and uppers is the cobbler's raw material.

clue.text: King Edmund so-called in derision, conceivably

indicators.note: the word could conceivably be reworked into another, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English king is given a nickname mockingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DERISION are rearranged, 'conceivably' signalling it. Edmund II of England was nicknamed for his bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund II, who fought the Danes in 1016, earned the byname for his toughness in battle.

clue.text: Horsey drink

definitions.meaning: the Suffolk ... is a breed of heavy draught horse
a mixed drink of spirits, fruit juice and spices served from a bowl

explanation.surface: A drink fit for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Suffolk breed of carthorse shares its name with a spiced mixed beverage served at parties.

clue.text: Appropriate to the nature of the beast, so to speak

definitions.text: Appropriate to the nature of the beast, so to speak

parts.words: Appropriate to the nature of the beast, so to speak
parts.note: 'so to speak' hints that the phrase is figurative: behaving true to one's personality

explanation.walkthrough: Behaviour consistent with someone's known personality is said to be true to type.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means consistent with a person's usual personality or typical behaviour.

clue.text: Restoration favourite sound as a bell

indicators.note: the word as spoken matches another spelling, so it is what the ear hears

parts.note: a bell tolling for a death rings a knell

explanation.surface: A favourite of the Restoration period is in perfect health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy. Nell Gwyn was Charles II's mistress; Charles II's reign is the Restoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell Gwyn, actress and mistress of Charles II, was the best-known royal favourite of that age.

clue.text: Almost convinced it's lovely and sound

parts.note: pretty means attractive or lovely
sure means sound, reliable

explanation.surface: Someone is fairly certain that something is both attractive and reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fairly certain is nearly, but not quite, convinced.

clue.text: Though fur covers it, the animal gets cold in an Eastern country

definitions.text: Though fur covers it, the animal

indicators.note: the cold word goes inside the country's name

parts.note: China is a country in the East
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: Despite its fur, a creature catches a chill in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the fact that the animal is prized for its dense fur.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American rodent with very soft, thick grey fur.

clue.text: Thumbing a lift to Herts town with a note

parts.note: Hitchin is a market town in Hertfordshire (Herts), England
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone hitchhikes to a Hertfordshire town carrying a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the short form of Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a free ride by holding out a thumb at the roadside is hitchhiking.

clue.text: Petty swindle has theologian in a scrape

indicators.note: the theologian goes inside the scraping tool

parts.note: a file is a tool for scraping or rasping
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

explanation.surface: A small fraud lands a churchman in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a scrape' looks like 'in trouble', but FILE, a rasp, is the scrape.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor dishonest scheme, such as fiddling expenses, is a small-scale cheat.

clue.text: Indication of ophidian seen in the Thames

parts.note: ophidian means snake-like; a boa is a snake
a trace is a sign or indication

explanation.surface: Signs of a snake have been spotted in the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oxford and Cambridge rowing contest is held each spring on the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual university rowing race between Oxford and Cambridge is held on London's river.

clue.text: Is within call for a revolting movement

indicators.note: one word is put within the other

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone is on the phone about a disgusting campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a rebellion, a movement of people in revolt.

clue.text: Wet or dry? Ay, there's the rub

definitions.text: Wet or dry? Ay, there's the rub

parts.words: Wet or dry? Ay, there's the rub
parts.note: Hamlet's 'there's the rub' (the difficulty) is read literally as a rubbing, of a hair wash that comes in wet or dry forms

explanation.walkthrough: The Hamlet quotation means 'that's the snag', but here the rub is a literal massage of the scalp.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair wash is rubbed into the scalp and comes as a liquid or as a dry powder.

clue.text: Shorten a kind of bridge

definitions.meaning: the standard form of the card game bridge, in which only tricks bid count towards game

explanation.surface: Make a bridge shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink something is to make it shorter, and the commonest bridge card game shares the name.

clue.text: In vindication he makes a number turn green

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number

indicators.note: the word is made to turn, so its letters change places

explanation.surface: A man seeking justice makes a figure go green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges GREEN into ENGER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exacts retribution for a wrong is a person seeking vindication.

clue.text: Temporary loss of activity by battery hens?

definitions.text: Temporary loss of activity by battery hens?

parts.words: Temporary loss of activity by battery hens?
parts.note: a temporary stoppage of work is read as caged hens ceasing to produce eggs

explanation.walkthrough: A temporary dismissal of workers is pictured as hens stopping egg production.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary suspension of workers or of activity is a break from producing.

clue.text: Instruct a political clique in transport

definitions.note: the definition describes a group of travellers riding in a vehicle

parts.note: to coach is to instruct
a party is a political group

explanation.surface: Someone teaches a group of politicians on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A group travelling together by bus on an outing are riding in road transport.

clue.text: About right, observe, in a withering way

indicators.note: one word goes about, or around, the other

parts.note: to see is to observe

explanation.surface: A remark about being right, delivered scornfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withering' here means drying up, not scornful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dried up and shrivelled, like autumn leaves, is withered.

clue.text: Prejudice good bowlers can handle

definitions.meaning: an unfair leaning for or against something
in lawn bowls the ball is weighted to curve, and skilled players use that swerve

explanation.surface: Skilled bowlers can cope with prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn bowls, played on a flat green, uses balls weighted on one side so they curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided leaning is unfairness, and in bowls it is the weighting that makes a bowl curve.

clue.text: Drive out twister pocketing 10p

indicators.note: the fish holds the other letters as if in its pocket

parts.note: an eel twists and wriggles
X is the Roman numeral ten and p the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Throw out a swindler who has pocketed ten pence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twister' looks like a cheat but is the wriggling EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone to leave is to eject them.

clue.text: Indulging in drunken gin beano…

indicators.note: the letters stagger about drunkenly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges at a gin-fuelled party.
explanation.walkthrough: A beano is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on a spree of excess is indulging heavily.

clue.text: … strictly calls for pints only

definitions.meaning: a drinker who never orders halves of beer

explanation.surface: Ordering only full pints of beer, strictly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: British beer is served in pints or half pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wholeheartedly without compromise, and a drinker who never asks for a half.
